meta.about: Access-control credential bit layouts, keyed by format ID rather than bit count. A bit count does not identify a layout: 32-bit alone has at least five mutually incompatible splits, 37-bit at least four, 36-bit at least four. Anything not listed here as 'implemented: true' is published for reference only and this package will not encode or decode it.

confidence.high: Two or more independent public sources agree, and the layout has been exercised against a real frame.
confidence.medium: A single third-party source, or sources that disagree on a detail. Treat as reference, not spec.
confidence.low: Field widths known, bit positions not published. Do not build hardware around it.

formats.name: HID H10301
formats.note: The de facto open standard. Parity intervals are 1-based bit numbers and exclude the parity bits themselves.
sources: emblemaccess: HID card numbers and facility codes

formats.name: HID H10306 / Honeywell N10002
formats.note: Both vendors use 16 facility + 16 card. This is NOT the only 34-bit layout - see awid-rs2-34.

formats.name: AWID RS2 34-bit
formats.note: Same bit count as H10306, different split. Feeding an RS2 card to a generic H10306 decoder yields a plausible but wrong facility code and card number. Parity bit positions were not published in the sources reviewed, so this package does not attempt it.
sources: accessgrid: AWID RS2 34bit - 8-bit site code, 24-bit card number

formats.name: Keyscan C15001
formats.note: Keyscan has never published C15001 bit positions. The bit map above is reconstructed from third-party sources, and third-party decoders have historically mislabelled C15001 reads (proxmark3 issue #1773). The 10-bit OEM field is the only field that lets a human sanity-check which layout was actually read - do not drop it.
sources: authoriz-id: Keyscan C1325 and C15001 36-bit guide
accessgrid: examples of every access control bit format

formats.name: Simplex S12906
formats.note: Publicly documented as a different 36-bit layout from C15001, but field positions were not available in the sources reviewed.

formats.name: AWID 36-bit
formats.note: Uses AWID's own modulation: standard HID-style readers cannot read it at all. Do not assume a 36-bit frame is C15001 just because the length matches.

formats.name: HID H10302
formats.note: No facility code at all - 35 bits of card number. Field layout is well attested; the parity boundary is not: Nedap and promptzero/pacs overlap the two 18-bit regions at bit 18, Suprema starts the odd region at bit 18. 35 data bits cannot be split evenly, which is where the disagreement comes from. Verify against a real frame before trusting either reading.

formats.name: HID H10304
formats.note: Same 37 bits as H10302, same vendor, completely different field split. A 37-bit frame alone cannot tell you which one it is - the user has to say. Same parity boundary dispute as H10302.
sources: tagtixrfid: H10301 vs H10302 vs H10304

formats.name: HID generic 37-bit
formats.note: Layout reported as two leading parity bits + 32-bit card number + one trailing parity bit. Field order comes from a single source group.

formats.name: PointGuard MDI 37-bit
formats.note: A 4-bit site code, so generic 37-bit decoders produce a facility code that is wrong by orders of magnitude.

formats.name: ATS 32-bit
formats.note: One of at least five 32-bit layouts. Included so that nobody mistakes '32-bit' for a format.

formats.name: Generic WIE32
formats.note: No parity bits at all - so a corrupted frame cannot be detected.

formats.name: Kantech K32
formats.note: 8 site + 16 card leaves 8 bits unaccounted for in the reviewed source.

formats.name: Nedap 32-bit
formats.note: 16 + 16 with no parity bits - the same split as H10306 but half the length, which is exactly the trap this dataset exists to document.

formats.name: Maxxess 32-bit
formats.note: 14 site + 16 badge, per the vendor's own application note.

formats.name: HID Corporate 1000
formats.note: Proprietary. Three parity bits whose coverage is interleaved (for example 4-5, 7-8, 10-11) rather than contiguous, so the simple 'continuous range' model used by most calculators cannot express it. The company code is assigned by HID to licensed buyers and is not publicly derivable.
